lead: Mother-to-child transmission happens in utero, in labour or through breast milk. Early lifelong ART with a suppressed viral load, infant prophylaxis and safe feeding reduce it to under 1%; untreated it is about 25%.
f: High viral load: the strongest factor · Low CD4, advanced disease, no ART, new infection in pregnancy · Prolonged ROM, chorioamnionitis, preterm birth, early ARM, scalp electrode · Mixed feeding, cracked nipples · Complications: miscarriage, PROM, preterm labour, opportunistic infection, TB, FGR

Opt-out testing at booking with syphilis and hepatitis B · Positive rapid test: confirm with a second, different test; retest late if at risk · Baseline CD4, viral load, Hb, creatinine, LFT, HBV, HCV, TB screen; test the partner

sc: Unbooked, in labour, status unknown → Rapid HIV test now

f: ART for all: start as soon as diagnosed (same day if ready), any CD4, any gestation, for life · TLD (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir) one tablet daily · Viral load 3 months after starting and at 34–36 wk (birth plan) · Cotrimoxazole 960 mg daily if CD4 ≤ 350 or WHO stage 3–4 · Avoid amniocentesis and CVS

sc: Diagnosed at 16 wk, CD4 500 → Start ART now, lifelong
tr: On cotrimoxazole: no SP for IPTp (two sulfa drugs; cotrimoxazole already prevents malaria)

f: The viral load decides · VL under 50 at 36 wk: vaginal birth, oral ART, no IV zidovudine · VL ≥ 1000 or unknown: elective CS at 38 wk + IV zidovudine (2 mg/kg over 1 h, then 1 mg/kg/h until the cord is clamped) · Continue oral ART through labour · Avoid early ARM, prolonged ROM, scalp electrodes, fetal blood sampling, routine episiotomy

sc: VL under 50, breech at 38 wk → Mode by obstetric reasons only

f: Wash, vitamin K, BCG, eye ointment · Low risk: nevirapine 15 mg daily for 6 wk · High risk (VL ≥ 1000, ART under 4 wk, found in labour): AZT + NVP 6 wk, then NVP 6 wk · Cotrimoxazole from 6 wk until HIV is excluded · DNA PCR at 6 wk and after weaning; antibody test only from 18 months

sc: Baby antibody positive at 9 months → Maternal antibody: do a PCR

f: Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months while the mother takes ART, then foods and continue to 12–24 months · No mixed feeding in the first 6 months · ART for life; viral load every 6–12 months · Contraception: all methods, plus condoms; efavirenz and rifampicin lower implant and pill levels · Four prongs: prevent HIV, family planning, stop MTCT, treat the family
